thesis: Alexandria Real Estate Equities (ARE) is a real estate investment trust that owns, operates, and develops life-science laboratory and office campuses in major U.S. innovation clusters (Greater Boston, San Francisco Bay Area, San Diego, Seattle, Maryland, Research Triangle, and New York City). **[Fact]** ARE trades on the NYSE. **[Fact]** FY2025 total revenue was **$2.95 billion** (down from **$3.05 billion** in FY2024) per `investor-documents/sec-edgar/10-K_20260126_rpt20251231_acc0001035443_26_000013.htm`. **[Fact]** FY2025 cash from operations was **$1.41 billion**, cash and equivalents **$549 million**, stockholders' equity **$15.47 billion**, and long-term debt approximately **$19.1 billion** (component proof; filing_facts XBRL tag pairing flagged low confidence on debt line). **[Fact]** Basic earnings per share were **$8.44** in FY2025 versus **$1.80** in FY2024, reflecting higher reported net income (**$1.43 billion** per filing_facts) that includes non-recurring items **[Inference]** not fully normalized in owner-cash math.
why_market_wrong: The stock may trade as a distressed levered life-science landlord after biotech funding slowed and vacancy rose, while the underlying campuses still generate substantial operating cash flow and development pipeline value. **[Inference]** FY2025 revenue fell **3.4%** year over year, so generalists may extrapolate occupancy pressure without crediting **$1.41 billion** of operating cash flow against a **$19 billion** debt stack that is typical for a large REIT capital structure. **[Inference]** Proof-first component math at base case sums to about **−$11.35** per share of filing-locked economic value versus a price near **$50**, suggesting the market prices asset recovery, lab-demand normalization, and refinancing flexibility beyond what the conservative component schedule captures today. **[Inference]** Activist filings (Greenlight, Eminence; context tier only) argue for capital-allocation and balance-sheet actions that are not in the base proof schedule.
